title: Apply for trader's plates
summary: This page provides information on how motor businesses can apply for trader's plates to drive unregistered vehicles for specific business purposes.
intro:
Trader's plates allow a motor business to drive an unregistered vehicle for purposes that are incidental to the manufacture, repair, or dealings of the vehicle, such as test driving, or moving a vehicle from one dealership to another.

Businesses issued with trader's plates include:

To apply for trader's plates, visit a Service NSW Centre.
who_can_apply: A motor business that needs to drive an unregistered vehicle for purposes incidental to the manufacture, repair, or dealings of the vehicle (e.g., test driving, moving a vehicle between dealerships).
what_you_need: Evidence of registration under business name (if applicable)
A copy of your motor industry licence
A copy or extract of your certificate of business registration or company name, ABN certificate
A detailed description on company letterhead of your business activities and the reasons why you need trader's plates
The name of the service centre where you will collect the plates
The completed PDF form: 'Trader's Plate Application'

how_to_steps.text: Make sure you have all your supporting documentation.
Visit a service centre and submit your application.

faqs.q: What are trader's plates used for?
faqs.a: Trader's plates allow a motor business to drive an unregistered vehicle for purposes incidental to the manufacture, repair, or dealings of the vehicle, such as test driving or moving a vehicle between dealerships.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for trader's plates?
faqs.a: You must visit a Service NSW Centre to apply for trader's plates.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to apply?
faqs.a: You need your proof of identity, business details, evidence of registration under a business name (if applicable), a copy of your motor industry licence, and a copy or extract of your certificate of business registration or company name, ABN certificate.
